'''Alexander Viktorovich Kabanov''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Александр Викторович Кабанов}}; born 27 March 1962 in Moscow, Soviet Union (now Russia)), is a Russian and American chemist, an educator, an entrepreneur, and a researcher in the fields of [[drug delivery]] and [[nanomedicine]].

== Biography and career ==
Kabanov was born in Moscow, USSR on 27 March 1962, in the family of Soviet chemist Viktor A. Kabanov.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=August 2006 |title=Victor Aleksandrovich Kabanov (1934–2006) |journal=Polymer Science Series A |language=en |volume=48 |issue=8 |pages=887–889 |doi=10.1134/S0965545X06080165 |issn=0965-545X|doi-access=free }}</ref> He graduated from the Faculty of Chemistry of the [[Moscow State University]] in 1984, where he also received PhD – [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate of Chemical Sciences]] in 1987 and D.Sc. – [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Chemical Sciences]] in 1990. In 1994 he reallocated to United States to the [[University of Nebraska Medical Center]] where he served on a faculty for nearly 18 years<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burbach |first=Karen |date=2007-03-07 |title=Meet Distinguished Scientist Alexander 'Sasha' Kabanov, Ph.D., Dr.Sc. |url=https://www.unmc.edu/newsroom/2007/03/07/meet-distinguished-scientist-alexander-sasha-kabanov-ph-d-dr-sc/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=Newsroom |language=en}}</ref> before moving to [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 2012. He is currently Mescal Swaim Ferguson Distinguished Professor at the [[UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy]], director of the Center for Nanotechnology in Drug Delivery and the Carolina Institute for Nanomedicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alexander V. Kabanov, Ph.D., Dr.Sci. |url=https://pharmacy.unc.edu/directory/kabanov/ |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy |language=en-US}}</ref>

Kabanov is a highly cited researcher<ref>{{Cite web |title=Publons.com |url=https://publons.com/wos-op/ |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=publons.com |language=en}}</ref> and as of January 2023 has over 47,000 citations with an [[h-index]] of 110.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Kabanov |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=PTouqvoAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> He published over 350 scientific papers and holds at least 36 US patents. He co-founded several pharmaceutical companies including Supratek Pharma Inc., SoftKemo, Bendarex and DelAQUA Pharmaceuticals. He trained over 70 graduate students and postdocs, half of whom are women and [[Underrepresented group|underrepresented minorities]] and 16 became faculty.<ref name=":0"/>

Kabanov was a founding director of the [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] [[Centers of Biomedical Research Excellence|Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (CoBRE)]] "Nebraska Center for Nanomedicine" and is the director of the NIH T32 Carolina Cancer Nanotechnology Training Program.<ref name=":0"/> He founded the Nanomedicine and Drug Delivery symposium series that has been held annually since 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NanoDDS2020 |url=http://www.nanodds.org/ |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=nanoDDS |language=en-US}}</ref> He is the editor-in-chief of the scientific journals Reviews and Advances in Chemistry (ReACh) and Doklady Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Reviews and Advances in Chemistry |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/13392/editorial-board |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Doklady Chemistry |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10631/editorial-board |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=ak |date=2025-12-18 |title=Summing up the year: from the Editor-in-Chief of the Reviews Journal of Chemistry (ReACh) and Doklady Сhemistry |url=https://t-invariant.org/2025/12/summing-up-the-year-from-the-editor-in-chief-of-the-reviews-journal-of-chemistry-reach-and-doklady-shemistry/ |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=Т-инвариант / T-invariant |language=en-US}}</ref>  He served a director-at-large of the Controlled Release Society (2019–2022), and is the past President (2018–2020) and the chief executive officer of the Russian American Science Association (RASA).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russian-American Science Association — Russian-American Science Association |url=https://rasa-usa.org/ |access-date=2023-01-20 |language=ru-RU}}</ref>

== Contributions to science==
Kabanov made broad impact to [[Pharmacy|pharmaceutical sciences]] and advanced polymer and colloidal sciences by developing novel methods using [[nanotechnology]] for the [[Drug delivery|therapeutic delivery]] of small drugs, [[nucleic acid]]s, and [[protein]]s. His early work was in the field of [[enzyme catalysis]] in [[surfactant]] aggregates in organic media,<ref>{{Cite book |title=Structure and reactivity in reverse micelles |date=1989 |publisher=Elsevier |others=M. P. Pileni |isbn=0-444-88166-2 |location=Amsterdam |oclc=20560416}}</ref> where he developed methods using reverse [[micelle]]s as nanoscale reactors for modification of proteins, controllable assembly of [[oligomer]]ic [[enzyme]]s and tailoring protein-polymer conjugates for [[Biological engineering|bioengineering]] applications.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kabanov |first1=A. Lee |last5=Bronich |first5=Tatiana K. |last6=Kabanov |first6=Alexander V. |last7=Gendelman |first7=Howard E. |year=2007 |title=A macrophage-nanozyme delivery system for Parkinson's disease |journal=Bioconjugate Chemistry |volume=18 |issue=5 |pages=1498–1506 |doi=10.1021/bc700184b |issn=1043-1802 |pmc=2677172 |pmid=17760417}}</ref> and macrophage-derived [[Exosome (vesicle)|exosomes]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haney |first1=Matthew J. |last2=Klyachko |first2=Natalia L. |last3=Zhao |first3=Yuling |last4=Gupta |first4=Richa |last5=Plotnikova |first5=Evgeniya G. |last6=He |first6=Zhijian |last7=Patel |first7=Tejash |last8=Piroyan |first8=Aleksandr |last9=Sokolsky |first9=Marina |last10=Kabanov |first10=Alexander V. |last11=Batrakova |first11=Elena V. |date=10 June 2015 |title=Exosomes as drug delivery vehicles for Parkinson's disease therapy |journal=Journal of Controlled Release|volume=207 |pages=18–30 |doi=10.1016/j.jconrel.2015.03.033 |issn=1873-4995 |pmc=4430381 |pmid=25836593}}</ref> for the delivery of therapeutic polypeptides and nucleic acids to the sites of [[inflammation]] in the brain to treat [[Neurological disorder|neurological diseases]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=neurons |first1=Scientists at UNC have developed methods to restore |last2=disease |first2=reduce the progression of Parkinson's |title=UNC researchers close to Parkinson's treatment |url=https://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2015/09/unc-researchers-close-to-parkinsons-treatment |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=The Daily Tar Heel |date=15 September 2015 }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
His honors include the [[Lenin Komsomol Prize]] (1988), the [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award|NSF Career award]] (1995), the RASA [[George Gamow]] award (2017), and the Controlled Release Society Founders award (2022).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Controlled Release Society 2022 Awards announced - Awards - Journal of Controlled Release - Journal - Elsevier |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-controlled-release/awards/journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-controlled-release/awards/controlled-release-society-2022-awards-announced |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> He was elected a member of [[Academia Europaea]] (2013), [https://academysciencesletters.org/ American Academy of Sciences and Letters] (2025), a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (2019),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jennings |first=Brittany |date=2019-11-27 |title=Professor becomes first Russian-American scientist elected to Russian Academy of Sciences |url=https://pharmacy.unc.edu/2019/11/professor-becomes-first-russian-american-scientist-elected-to-russian-academy-of-sciences/ |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy |language=en-US}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (2015),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander V. Kabanov, Ph.D., Dr.Sc. COF-1817 - AIMBE |url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-1817/ |access-date=2023-01-30 |language=en}}</ref> the [[National Academy of Inventors]] (2017),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendenhall |first=Grayson |date=2017-12-12 |title=Kabanov Elected to National Academy of Inventors |url=https://pharmacy.unc.edu/2017/12/kabanov-elected-national-academy-inventors/ |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy |language=en-US}}</ref> the Controlled Release Society (2018), and [https://academysciencesletters.org/ the] [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2021).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jared |first=H. |date=2022-01-28 |title=AAAS honors 4 faculty as fellows |url=https://thewell.unc.edu/2022/01/28/4-named-2021-aaas-fellows/ |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=The Well |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Public position ==
Kabanov has taken public position against the use of [[chemical weapon]]s<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willingham |first=Emily |title=Gel Packed with Chemical "Scavengers" Protects against Sarin Gas |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gel-packed-with-chemical-scavengers-protects-against-sarin-gas/ |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-01 |title=Scientists petition to end political persecution in Russia |url=https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/scientists-petition-to-end-political-persecution-in-russia/13322224 |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=ABC Radio National |language=en-AU}}</ref> and in 2021 co-authored a petition signed by nearly a thousand Russian-speaking scientists demanding [[Government of Russia|Russian authorities]] to end political prosecution of [[Alexei Navalny]] and his supporters, investigate [[Poisoning of Alexei Navalny|his poisoning]] and turn to international cooperation to confront global threats,<ref name="pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov">{{Cite journal |last1=Kabanov |first1=Alexander |last2=Krasnok |first2=Alex |last3=Seletskiy |first3=Denis |year=2021 |title=Russia: scientists petition to end political persecution |journal=Nature |volume=591 |issue=7849 |page=202 |bibcode=2021Natur.591..202K |doi=10.1038/d41586-021-00594-y |issn=1476-4687 |pmid=33664514 |s2cid=232124322}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title='The situation could well lead to a catastrophe' More than 100 scientists and scholars, including Nobel laureates, sign open letter demanding that Russia stop persecuting activists and turn instead to international cooperation |url=https://meduza.io/en/feature/2021/02/02/the-situation-could-well-lead-to-a-national-uprising |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=Meduza |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-12 |title=The legacy of Andrei Sakharov and the state of Russian science today |language=en-AU}}</ref> On 24 February 2022, Kabanov signed an open letter of Russian scientists and journalists against the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|war in Ukraine]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Открытое письмо российских ученых и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной – Т-инвариант / T-invariant |date=24 February 2022 |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2026, following the designation of RASA as "[[Russian undesirable organizations law|undesirable organization]]" Kabanov was designated "[[Russian foreign agent law|foreign agent]]", along with several other RASA members.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Krylov |first1=Anna |last2=Efimov |first2=Igor |date=2026-04-29 |title=When Science Becomes 'Undesirable': A Case for Supporting
